page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highcpu-48 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance featuring 48 vCPUs and 96 GB of RAM. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor with an x86_64 architecture, the server provides 24 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled running at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The hardware configuration allocates a dedicated CPU model with a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It features advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions for accelerated mathematical and matrix operations. The instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong performance in compute-heavy workloads. The server achieves top-tier results in Geekbench image processing and text processing, alongside strong performance in Geekbench single-core and multi-core metrics. Passmark CPU tests, including extended instructions, encryption, and physics, consistently place in the strong performance tier. For data compression, single-threaded gzip compression and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression show high throughput. Memory performance is moderate, with a read-only cached small block bandwidth of 3206.74 GB/sec and uncached large block write bandwidth of 64.01 GB/sec.

The c4-highcpu-48 is highly suited for compute-intensive tasks that leverage vector and matrix extensions, such as CPU-based machine learning inference, image processing, and high-throughput web serving. In LLM inference benchmarks, the instance demonstrates strong prompt processing speeds across small, medium, and large models, and top-tier text generation speeds for small models. Given the 2.0 GB of RAM per core ratio and the lack of local storage, the instance offers high resource density for pure compute tasks, making it a cost-efficient choice for workloads that do not require massive memory footprints or local disk I/O.
